remarks.text:
Thank you all for your replies!

Just sent @bot codes to a bunch of you — a few use cases that stood out:

For growth & clients:
→ Find leads, draft outreach, and turn wins into case studies @kouroshbaloo
→ Build a competitor comparison matrix with sources @PaulWeissAI

For ops & shipping:
→ Monitor hundreds of ad accounts and catch broken signup/payment flows @yashjain10k
→ Watch Jira, flag blockers, and draft the weekly status update @partykma
→ Triage support tickets, draft replies, and escalate with full context @jurlycat
→ For hotel owners: regularly test the booking flow so website booking errors get caught @LeenCanvas
→ Automate paperwork and back-office workflows for an electrical contracting business @kerwinv101

For research & content:
→ Monitor AI builders on X, verify sources, then turn wins into hooks and scripts @jenni489471
→ A research desk for AI that turns noise into a daily brief @Orynsky

Will run this again if I get more codes. Meanwhile consider subscribing to my YouTube below :)
https://t.co/SKvvXlY6Km

remarks.name: Aaron Levie
remarks.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
remarks.text:
There’s a massive chasm between the power of AI models and the ultimate workflows that enterprises are trying to automate. This gap is the opportunity for the applied AI layer to fill. 

You need to connect the intelligence to workflows, often reengineer processes, aggregate the right context and data, allow for the right human in the loop experiences, drive change management, do domain specific evals, manage the security and governance of the data and process, and much more.

We’re going to see this layer emerge in every vertical and horizontal category. And ironically, even as models improve at incredible rates, this layer still must exist - and may become even more important and useful. Greater capability enables even more complex tasks to be tackled, amplifying the challenges if you don’t do this well.

Was super fun chatting with @sonyatweetybird on all the things going into AI diffusion.
remarks.translation: AI模型的力量与企业试图自动化的最终工作流程之间，存在着巨大的鸿沟。这一差距正是应用型AI层需要填补的机遇。你需要将智能连接到工作流程中，往往还要重新设计流程，聚合正确的上下文与数据，提供恰到好处的“人在回路”体验，推动变革管理，进行特定领域的评估，管理数据与流程的安全性和治理，等等。我们将看到这一层在每一个垂直和水平类别中涌现。而且颇具讽刺意味的是，即使模型以惊人的速度不断改进，这一层依然必须存在——甚至可能变得更加重要和有用。更强的能力使得更复杂的任务得以被攻克，但如果你在这一层做得不好，挑战也会被放大。与@sonyatweetybird聊AI扩散所涉及的所有事情，真的非常有趣。

remarks.name: Peter Yang
remarks.role: Practical AI tutorials and interviews for busy people
remarks.text:
The Grok @bot team asked me if I had any advice for solopreneurs.

I’ve only been doing this full time for three months, but my advice is to design your business so you can spend more time doing work you actually enjoy.

There will always be choices that could make more money. But if those choices leave you doing work you don’t enjoy, then that defeats the purpose of becoming a solopreneur in the first place.

Delegate that boring work to your bots instead or just don't do it :)

Was super fun joining the @SpaceXAI live stream this morning, the team is still going strong here: https://t.co/u2qwydK7M8
remarks.translation: Grok @bot团队问我，对独立创业者有什么建议。我全职做这个才三个月，但我的建议是，设计你的业务，让你能把更多时间花在真正喜欢的工作上。总会有一些选择能赚更多钱。但如果这些选择让你去做不喜欢的工作，那就违背了当初成为独立创业者的初衷。把那些无聊的工作交给你的机器人，或者干脆别做 :) 今早加入@SpaceXAI直播特别开心，团队在这里依然势头强劲：https://t.co/u2qwydK7M8

remarks.name: Thariq
remarks.role: Claude Code anthropicai. prev YC W20, spc, medialab
remarks.text:
I was not expecting things to go this way, but I think MCPs are better than CLIs for most integrations. 

The models have gotten much better at tool calling, we can defer tools & MCP is now stateless.

If you need to compose/filter data, add params like query to your MCP tools.
remarks.translation: 我没想到事情会这样发展，但我认为对于大多数集成来说，MCP 比 CLI 更好。模型在工具调用方面已经进步了很多，我们可以延迟加载工具，而且 MCP 现在是无状态的。如果你需要组合/过滤数据，可以在你的 MCP 工具中添加像 query 这样的参数。

podcasts.originalTitle: 🔬“We have foundation models for language, not for physics” — Anima Anandkumar, Bren Professor of Computing
podcasts.excerpt: 几年前，加州理工学院教授、Accelerated Understanding联合创始人Anima Anandkumar着手开发首个基于AI的开源天气模型。在与该领域专家交流时，她遭遇了质疑。天气是混沌的，物理模拟很难，已经发展了几十年，而且需要超级计算机，数据根本不够。尽管有这些保留意见，Anima还是坚持前行并着手构建。不到一年，她的团队就开发出了FourCastNet，一个能与现有最佳物理模拟相媲美的预测模型。多亏了Anima及其后续工作，现在任何人都可以使用消费级GPU在短时间尺度上准确预测天气。在我们发布的约十五期科学类节目中，<a target="_blank" href="http://latent.…
podcasts.originalExcerpt: A few years ago, Caltech Prof. and co-founder of Accelerated Understanding, Anima Anandkumar set out to develop the first open-source weather model with AI. Talking to experts in the field, she was met with skepticism. Weather is chaotic, physics simulations are hard, have been developed for decades, and require supercomputers, the data just isn’t there. Despite reservations, Anima went forth and built. Within a year her team had developed FourCastNet, a predictive model that is competitive with the best physics-based simulations available. Thanks to Anima, and her follow up work, anyone can now predict weather accurately over a short timescale using consumer grade GPUs.
